documentClass: independent adversarial review of a coordinator decision draft
reviewMode: Refute, do not confirm. Every cited digest recomputed from live bytes. Every live-state claim checked against live file 08, live COORD, live git, and the frozen artifacts themselves. No claim accepted on the draft's own assertion.
independence: The other reviewer's D-250 output was not read. docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-250.review-adversarial.codex.json was observed to exist by directory listing only; its bytes were never opened and its verdict is unknown and not inferred. Prior-cycle reviews (D-208, D-249) were read for structural convention only, which is a different cycle and not this cycle's other reviewer.
decision: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 2 SHOULD-FIX. CONSENT is available only at zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. Every one of the eighteen dispatched attacks is REFUTED; the draft's substantive record is accurate in every particular I could measure. Both SHOULD-FIX findings are evidentiary-discipline defects in the same family: the draft asserts four cross-gate live-state currency findings that it never measures and never protects, and its reversibility clause omits the cross-gate decision whose output it recites as current.

shouldFix.field: Measured inputs table (lines 66-80) and remeasurement clause (lines 82-87), against the live-remasurement recital at lines 102-105
shouldFix.text: leftover-join.v8 leftoverDesign `[]` remains the current G23 leftover-join. leftover-join.v4 (G23) is not current. leftover-join.v5 remains the current G25 leftover-join. leftover-join.v4 (G25) remains split.
shouldFix.finding: These four sentences sit inside the block headed 'Live remasurement at draft time:' — the draft's own designated register of measured live-state findings. They are therefore presented to a later reader as measured. They are not measured. The Measured inputs table carries eleven rows and none of them is g23-leftover-join.v8.json, g23-leftover-join.v4.json, g25-leftover-join.v5.json, or g25-leftover-join.v4.json. I recomputed all four from live bytes — 498324e5e456562317c7681b44cdac9138ca1e947aa363dad5a331caa3eef812, a542dc6b023d07cf8657c76909ded1641efd29277760308d52574fa706fad56e, 9f2b137fe0b01830b4113ef26c8283214a75982f588f164391d61c5510f67aa3, 441fd35afc9c6bd13bec54271a5bcd5e4feb0e263aee391aa1d0dd41b5086e15 — and grepped each of the four digests against the full 166 lines of the draft. All four return zero occurrences. The remeasurement clause compounds this. Its trigger is 'If a cited file moves', and its protected set is enumerated as 'file 08, leftover-join v3, leftover-join.v4, occupancy v3, occupancy v1, both Stage A verdicts, and this draft'. None of the four G23/G25 artifacts is in that set, and because no baseline digest for them was ever recorded, 'moves' is not evaluable for them at all. The four recitals are consequently outside remeasurement protection by construction, not by oversight of the clause's wording.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The Measured inputs table plus the remeasurement clause are jointly the mechanism by which this corpus keeps an adopted entry's live-state recitals true at the moment of adoption rather than merely true when the draft was typed. A recital inside that mechanism's scope but outside its coverage is the one shape the mechanism cannot catch: if g23-leftover-join.v8.json or g25-leftover-join.v5.json were rewritten between this draft and adoption, the clause would not fire, no reviewer would be directed to remasure, and D-250 would enter the permanent record asserting a false currency finding about a gate it does not govern. The exposure is not hypothetical for this cycle specifically — D-249, adopted at HEAD one commit ago, rewrote the G25 leftover-join lineage that line 104 now recites.
shouldFix.conventionEvidence: The directly analogous adopted precedent is D-249, the immediately preceding entry, same decision type (leftover remasurement), same reviewer pair, adopted at HEAD 1e939c5. D-249 recited a strictly smaller cross-gate surface than D-250 — G23 only, not G23 and G25 — and it measured that surface completely. Its Measured inputs table carries 'Frozen leftover-join.v8 (D-240; current G23 leftover-join; not this subject)' and 'Frozen leftover-join.v4 (G23; D-198; not current; not this subject)' with digests, and its remeasurement clause names 'leftover-join.v8, leftover-join.v4 (G23)' in the unmoved set. D-250 recites more and measures less. The asymmetry is sharper still on the corpus's own stated truncation rule: the D-249 claude2 review recorded the settled convention as 'the version tail is truncated below the load-bearing predecessors', omitting non-load-bearing versions. D-250 inverts it. It spends two table rows on G24 leftover-join.v1 and v2 (lines 74-75), which appear nowhere else in the draft and are recited by nothing, while dropping all four cross-gate artifacts that its live-remasurement block does recite. The table carries its least load-bearing entries and drops its most load-bearing ones.
shouldFix.notAMustFix: Every one of the four recitals is true at draft time and I verified each independently, which is why this is SHOULD-FIX and not MUST-FIX. g23-leftover-join.v8.json summary.leftoverDesign is []; D-240 is the newest G23 leftover-join recording in COORD, so v8 is current and the G23 v4 of D-198 is not; D-249 is the newest G25 leftover-join recording, so g25-leftover-join.v5.json is current; and g25-leftover-join.v5.json itself records the v4 disposition as 'split Claude REJECT 0/2 G25LJ-V4-CL-SF1/SF2 / Codex ACCEPT 0/0 and is not current'. The defect is that the entry asserts these as measured findings without measuring them, not that it asserts them falsely.
shouldFix.remedy: Add the four artifacts to the Measured inputs table with the digests recomputed above, and add leftover-join.v8, leftover-join.v4 (G23), leftover-join.v5 and leftover-join.v4 (G25) to the remeasurement clause's unmoved set — reproducing the D-249 shape. Alternatively, if the cross-gate recitals are intended as non-load-bearing context rather than measured findings, move lines 102-105 out of the 'Live remasurement at draft time' block so they are not presented as measured. Either repair closes the finding; the first matches precedent.

shouldFix.text: Does not unwrite D-150, D-199, D-224, or D-249.
shouldFix.finding: The non-unwrite list is written as a closed enumeration and omits D-240. D-240 is 'Record g23-leftover-join.v8 as G23 leftover remasurement' — the decision that made leftover-join.v8 the current G23 leftover-join, which is precisely the standing line 102 recites as live and which line 37 protects with a dedicated doesNot ('Does not record leftover-join.v4 (G23) as current G23 leftover-join'). The entry thus leans on D-240's output in two separate places while declining to name D-240 among the decisions it does not unwrite. The other four cross-gate and lineage dependencies are all named: D-150 is the naming parent, D-199 the predecessor G24 leftover-join recording, D-224 the occupancy v3 recording, and D-249 both the prior decision and the G25 v5 recording that line 104 recites. D-240 is the single dependency in the recital set with no corresponding entry in the reversibility list.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The non-unwrite list is how an adopted entry fixes the blast radius of its own overturn. C-D250 is the declared overturn handle; a later actor executing it reads this list to determine what must survive. An omitted dependency is a dependency the overturn is not told to preserve, and the omitted one here governs a different gate entirely, so the damage would land outside G24 where this entry's reviewers are looking.
shouldFix.conventionEvidence: I measured the reversibility clause of every leftover-remasurement entry in the current run: D-240 ('Does not unwrite D-147, D-223, D-237, D-238, or D-239'), D-242 ('D-086, D-145, D-196, D-218, or D-241'), D-244 ('D-145, D-196, D-218, D-241, D-242, or D-243'), D-246 ('D-145, D-196, D-218, D-241, D-243, D-244, or D-245'), D-248 ('D-145, D-196, D-218, D-241, D-243, D-245, D-246, or D-247'), and D-249 ('D-151, D-200, D-225, D-240, or D-248'). The settled shape is naming parent, same-lineage predecessor recordings, occupancy recording, prior decision, and any cross-gate recording the entry recites. D-249 is decisive: it is the only other entry in this run that recites a cross-gate leftover-join, it recites exactly leftover-join.v8, and it names exactly D-240 in its non-unwrite list for that reason. D-250 recites the same artifact and drops the same decision.

acceptanceStatement: CONSENT is available only at zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. Two SHOULD-FIX findings stand, so the verdict is OBJECT. The objection is narrow and repairable in a turn 2 draft: add the four cross-gate artifacts to the Measured inputs table and to the remeasurement clause's unmoved set, and add D-240 to the reversibility non-unwrite list.
